facts.raw_span: purpuric lesions on her face, elbows, knees, and feet
dusky purpuric macules and patches on her nose, bilateral cheeks, forehead, and left ear
reticulated purpuric macules and patches on her knees, feet, and the extensor surfaces of her arms
skin sloughing off the lesions on her elbows and knees
Hypercalcemia (calcium level, 11.5 mg/dL)
Acute kidney injury (creatinine level, 5.6 mg/dL)
Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels (cryocrit, 16%)
Negative results for hepatitis, antinuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies
multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi with relatively little vessel wall inflammation

concepts.why: The patient has elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis, and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear, which are characteristic of cryoglobulinemia.
The patient has purpuric lesions on her face, elbows, knees, and feet, which are consistent with vasculitis.

The patient has an abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses, monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis, and hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells, which are characteristic of multiple myeloma.
The patient has elevated creatinine levels, which indicate acute kidney injury.
The patient has elevated calcium levels, which are consistent with hypercalcemia.
The patient has a history of chronic kidney disease and elevated creatinine levels, which indicate renal impairment.

The patient has an abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses and monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis, which are characteristic of plasma cell dyscrasia.
The patient has multifocal intravascular fibrinoid material consisting of a mix of cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi, which is consistent with intravascular fibrinoid material.

rationales.F01: Purpuric lesions are a common manifestation of cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F05: Hypercalcemia is often associated with multiple myeloma.
rationales.F06: Acute kidney injury can be a complication of multiple myeloma and cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F07: Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear are characteristic of cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F08: Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses is a hallmark of plasma cell dyscrasias, including multiple myeloma.
rationales.F09: Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis is a specific finding for multiple myeloma and cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F10: Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels are a diagnostic criterion for cryoglobulinemia.
rationales.F12: Intravascular fibrinoid material is a characteristic histopathological finding in cryoglobulinemia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of purpuric lesions, hypercalcemia, and abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses, along with the bone marrow biopsy showing 80% plasma cells with atypical morphology and κ-light-chain restriction, strongly supports the diagnosis of Multiple myeloma, which can also explain the secondary Cryoglobulinemia.
